verbalization: Tolazoline, a member of the xylometazoline family, exhibits structural similarities to Tymazoline and Xylometazoline, both of which bind to Adra2c. The shared structural features between Tolazoline and Xylometazoline, along with their common ancestry as organic molecular entities, suggest a potential mechanism of action involving Adra2c. The lowest common ancestor of Tolazoline and Xylometazoline, as well as their shared classification as adrenergic agents, supports a functional link between these compounds and Adra2c. The evidence indicates that Tolazoline may act as an adrenergic antagonist by binding to Adra2c, potentially through a similar mechanism as its structural relatives. This relationship is further supported by the observed binding of Xylometazoline to Adra2c, reinforcing the hypothesis that Tolazoline shares a similar pharmacological profile. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible role for Tolazoline in modulating adrenergic signaling through its interaction with Adra2c.
